subject: Mixture of fixed and free variances in multi-group growth model

messages.author: d2097a307b83cbc3
messages.subject: Mixture of fixed and free variances in multi-group growth model
parts:
Hello,

I'm trying to use Lavaan 0.5-15 to estimate a growth model with two groups where most of the variances are free but a few (one in each group) are fixed to 0.

Using the following model as an example (propToll.0, propToll.1., etc. are continuous variables ranging from 0 to 1):

i =~ 1*propToll.0 + 1*propToll.1 + 1*propToll.2 + 1*propToll.3 + 1*propToll.4
s =~ 0*propToll.0 + c(l1_1,l1_2)*propToll.1 + c(l2_1,l2_2)*propToll.2 + start(c(5,5))*propToll.3 + c(l3_1,l3_2)*propToll.3 + 4*propToll.4
propToll.0 ~~ start(c(0,1))*propToll.0 + c(0, v0_2)*propToll.0
propToll.3 ~~ start(c(1,0))*propToll.3 + c(v3_1, 0)*propToll.3
i ~ i*1

When I run this model with the mimic="MPlus" option, the variances of propToll.0 and propToll.3 in both groups are free, but equal and with the same label (v0_2 and v3_1 respectively). If I run it without the mimic="MPlus" option, then the variances of propToll.0 and propToll.3 in both groups are free and not equal but the variances of propToll.0 and propToll.3 are labelled as v0_2 and v3_1 in group 1 and not labelled at all in group 2. I am also able to fix the variances in both groups to different values.

Is there a way for me to fix the variances for only one group to zero while leaving the variance in the other group free?

Thank you for your help.

Richard

messages.subject: Re: Mixture of fixed and free variances in multi-group growth model
parts:
On 11/25/2013 02:56 AM, Richard Ellison wrote:
> Hello,
>
> I'm trying to use Lavaan 0.5-15 to estimate a growth model with two
> groups where most of the variances are free but a few (one in each
> group) are fixed to 0.
>
> Using the following model as an example (propToll.0, propToll.1., etc.
> are continuous variables ranging from 0 to 1):
>
> i =~ 1*propToll.0 + 1*propToll.1 + 1*propToll.2 + 1*propToll.3 +
> 1*propToll.4
> s =~ 0*propToll.0 + c(l1_1,l1_2)*propToll.1 + c(l2_1,l2_2)*propToll.2 +
> start(c(5,5))*propToll.3 + c(l3_1,l3_2)*propToll.3 + 4*propToll.4
> propToll.0 ~~ start(c(0,1))*propToll.0 + c(0, v0_2)*propToll.0
> propToll.3 ~~ start(c(1,0))*propToll.3 + c(v3_1, 0)*propToll.3
> i ~ i*1
>
> When I run this model with the mimic="MPlus" option, the variances of
> propToll.0 and propToll.3 in both groups are free, but equal and with
> the same label (v0_2 and v3_1 respectively). If I run it without the
> mimic="MPlus" option, then the variances of propToll.0 and propToll.3 in
> both groups are free and not equal but the variances of propToll.0 and
> propToll.3 are labelled as v0_2 and v3_1 in group 1 and not labelled at
> all in group 2. I am also able to fix the variances in both groups to
> different values.
>
> Is there a way for me to fix the variances for only one group to zero
> while leaving the variance in the other group free?

Yes. But you can not mix 'labels' and 'fixed parameter values' in the
same modifier. But you can repeat the same term with different
'modifiers', for example;

propToll.0 ~~ start(c(0,1))*propToll.0 + c(v0_1, v0_2)*propToll.0 + c(0,
NA)*propToll.0

Here we have three times the term 'propToll.0' on the left hand side of
the "~~" operator. The first modifier is for the starting values, the
second for the labels, and the third for fixing/freeing parameters.

Yves.

Thank you, I knew I had to be missing something. This is a better solution than only setting the labels then using complex constraints ('=') to set the fixed parameters.

Richard
